memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You are a lion's cub, Judah; you return from the prey, my son. Like a lion he crouches and lies down, like a lioness—who dares to rouse him?'" — Gen 49:9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Judah is a lion. Not a frightened animal, not a cub hiding, but a lion at rest — the picture of settled, unthreatened strength. Who dares to rouse him?

This image would follow Judah's tribe through the whole Bible. And in the very last book of Scripture, John weeps because no one is found worthy to open the scroll, until an elder says to him: "Do not weep! See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed" (Rev 5:5).

Jacob's dying words about his son point forward, across centuries, to Jesus Christ.

But notice what happens next in Revelation. John turns to look at the Lion — and sees a Lamb, looking as if it had been slain. The Lion conquers as a Lamb. Strength that saves comes through sacrifice.

That is the heart of the gospel. Our Lord is genuinely the Lion, and no power in the universe can rouse or overturn Him. And He won His victory not by crushing His enemies but by laying down His life for them.

If Christ is yours, this Lion is on your side, and He is at rest. Nothing can pluck you from His hand.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does it mean to you that Christ is both Lion and Lamb?
2. Are you living as though your Saviour is anxious, or at rest?
3. What are you afraid of that the Lion of Judah has already overcome?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the Lion of the tribe of Judah who conquered as a slain Lamb. Thank You that Your victory is settled and my safety rests in You. Amen.
